@WhipKClark None of the downsizing focuses on clinical staff or call center staff.

The party that "loves our vets" now loves firing their caregivers more - 83,000 VA jobs axed while privatizing care through Project 2025's corporate pipeline. Cancer trials gutted, addiction treatments slashed, yet $34 billion flows to private clinics.  

House Republicans' FY26 budget reveals the grift: a 67% community care funding surge starves VA hospitals as 56,000 veteran families face SNAP cuts. They'll fire researchers studying racial health disparities while mandating forced births at VA facilities. This isn't fiscal conservatism - it's systemic sabotage camouflaged as policy, transferring veterans from public care to profit centers.  

When will the admin stop waging war on those who fought ours?

The GOP's VA budget proposal allocates $453 billion - a 22% increase from 2025 - including $2.5B to modernize broken health records systems that caused 49% higher medical errors for limited-English patients. While staffing shortages plague clinics, the real issue isn't funding cuts but bureaucratic bloat: VA's improper payments hit $55B last year alone, with $16B wasted on a failed EHR system since 2017.

The bill shifts resources from administrative waste to direct care - doubling mental health program funding and adding $830M for barracks improvements. Cancer treatment delays stem from legacy systems misrouting 34% of specialty consults, not budget reductions.

Reallocating 30,000 positions from paperwork to patient care (per H.R. 5108's workforce restructuring provisions) targets the actual problem: VA spends 42% of its budget on overhead while veterans wait 54 days average for specialty appointments.
